findings.description: jwt.decode only base64-decodes the token and does not verify the signature, so SECRET is never used. Anyone can forge a token. Also, claims may be null for a malformed token, and claims.sub then throws a TypeError, which goes to next(err) and returns a 500.
findings.scenario: Send 'Authorization: Bearer <unsigned token with sub=adminId>'. The request is authenticated as that user.
findings.fix: Use jwt.verify(token, SECRET, { algorithms: ['HS256'] }) and return 401 if it throws.

findings.description: `req.user.role = 'admin'` assigns instead of comparing. The condition is always truthy, so every authenticated user passes and their role is overwritten to admin (and persisted if the user object is saved).
findings.scenario: A regular user calls any admin-only route. They are allowed through, and the 403 branch is unreachable.

findings.description: forEach with an async callback does not await the deletes. The handler responds before the deletions finish, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Sessions may remain active even though the response reports them as revoked.
findings.scenario: The client receives {revoked: N} while the deletes are still in flight or have failed. A failed delete crashes the process or silently leaves the session valid.

findings.description: revokeSessions uses req.params.id with no check that the caller owns that account or is an admin. It also has no try/catch, so a DB error becomes an unhandled rejection in Express 4 and the request hangs.
findings.scenario: Any authenticated user calls the endpoint with another user's id and revokes that user's sessions.
findings.fix: Require req.user.id === req.params.id or an admin role, and wrap the handler in try/catch that calls next(err).

findings.description: The limit is not capped. A caller can pass a huge limit, and a negative value is accepted as well. Only the first `limit` sessions are revoked, so the endpoint does not revoke all sessions.
findings.scenario: limit=1 revokes one session and the others stay valid. limit=1000000000 loads an unbounded number of rows.
findings.fix: Revoke all sessions for the user with a single deleteByUser call, or clamp limit to a sane range and loop.

findings.description: SECRET is exported from the auth module, which widens the exposure of the signing key.
findings.scenario: Any module that requires this file can read or log the JWT signing secret.
